translations.answer: Cannot continue using q.tail(na) to subtract element-wise from the reference. The implementation of PR #161 has been merged first, distinguishing between the joint configuration dimension nq_actuated and the actuator velocity dimension na. A neutral configuration is used to construct an augmented reference including the root, with the joint reference written at the end. The function pinocchio::difference(model, ref_augmented, q) is then called, and the final na elements of the velocity space error are extracted. This PR also includes a pose convergence test with a model containing spherical joints.
translations.applicability: Applicable to systems with spherical or continuous joints where nq != nv, and using the implementation of PR #161 in the TSID. The nq_actuated assumption must be rechecked for custom root joints.
translations.credibility.rationale: The issue has been closed, the environment is clear and there is no conflict. The reference is formally documented and has independent reproducibility with exact citation.
translations.details.attempts.0: The discussion first clarifies that the pose reference should not include a floating base. The maintainers suggest constructing an augmented reference with a floating base configuration, performing a complete model difference, and then extracting the joint portion. The ball joints or continuous joints should use the Pinocchio manifold difference instead of element-wise subtraction.
translations.details.diagnostics.0: Compare model.nq, model.nv, robot.na with joint type; check whether the pose reference is in configuration space or velocity space; use Pinocchio manifold difference for ball joints or continuous joints instead of element-wise subtraction.
translations.details.effective_fixes.0: Use merged PR #161: RobotWrapper explicitly saves nq_actuated/is_fixed_base; use neutral configuration to construct augmented reference, write joint reference in the tail; compute pinocchio::difference(model, ref_augmented, q) and take the last na velocity space error.
translations.details.environments.0: TSID old submission b0d6bff; problem covers revolute unbounded joint and spherical joint; PR #161's test model includes spherical joint, fixed base test shows nq != nv.
translations.details.limits.0: PR treats nq_actuated for floating base as nq-7; custom root joint or other configuration should still verify this assumption and target TSID version.
translations.details.outcomes.0: PR #161 merged on 2022-04-11; patch adds 7-DoF model with spherical joint, requiring error monotonic decrease and reach 1e-8 in up to 1000 pose tasks; original author then closed Issue via PR merged.
translations.details.problem_statements.0: Why can't TaskJointPosture on robots with nq != nv use q.tail(na) and element-wise subtraction to calculate pose error?
translations.details.suspected_causes.0: The old implementation assumed that all joints except the root joint satisfy nq = nv, and used the joint configuration clipping length and executor velocity dimension na in a mixed manner.
translations.details.symptoms.0: The configuration vector has an incorrect dimension when clipped according to na, and the difference(q1, q2) of the manifold configuration is not equal to q2 - q1, leading to incorrect calculation of the pose task error.
